This waits for a person at Theorem to decide whether the AddressSanitizer exemption should be wider. I found no blocking item.

**For a person at Theorem to decide:** on `main`, the allocator shim that the pinned Rust toolchain writes is a finding. With this change, `is_rust_allocator_shim` also accepts:

- the v0 spelling of each shim name in a crate named `__rustc`, with any `s<base-62>_` disambiguator (`RUSTC_V0`, head `tools/check_links.py:114`);
- two more names: `__rust_no_alloc_shim_is_unstable_v2` and `__rust_alloc_error_handler_should_panic_v2` (head `tools/check_links.py:111-112`).

These rules don't change: the code must make no memory access, at most one member is exempt, and every function of any binding must be one of the shim's. The person decides whether the `asan` and `asan-ubsan` builds may link an object with these names uninstrumented, as a `rust-allocator-shim` entry in the `uninstrumented` list. The description says that tessera-sort's enrollment (#⁠170) needs this.

Not blocking: the docstring of `is_rust_allocator_symbol` says "a global function", but `is_rust_allocator_shim` calls it on every function of any binding (head `tools/check_links.py:825` and `846`).
